guide: Open Start and type your imprint name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the smallest gap between two releases, how many calendar entries you can carry in a month and how old a store price check may be.

Write every title in Titles: pen name, series, book number, words, pages, release date, status and the ebook copies a month from your sales sheet. Months on sale, days to release and open jobs fill in by themselves.
Write every edition in Editions: format, list price, unit cost, royalty share (check each store's current terms), identifier and pages or finished hours. The royalty per copy fills in.
Keep the series in Series and Series Plan Steps: one row per book with its planned or actual release, planned cost and the read-through you expect into the next book.
Add the production jobs to Contractor Deadlines and the price promotions to Promotion Dates. They appear on the Release Calendar with the dates that matter.
Fill the Release Calendar with releases, pre-order openings, planned editions, promotions and deadlines. The conflict check flags two releases closer than your smallest gap.
Check Release Gaps, Calendar by Month and Edition Completeness Check each month: they show gaps under the minimum, busy months and editions with a missing or duplicated identifier.
Enter the price on each store in Store Price List and the day you checked it. The sheet shows prices that differ from the list price and checks that are too old.
Use Title Format Coverage, Format Wish List and Price per Page to decide which format to add next and what a print price should be.
Use the 18 tools to test a release date, build a series timeline, find the date to start the next book, rank missing formats and check that a pre-order is safe.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.

Read the Catalogue Dashboard and the charts every week. A first-time author with one to three books can use most sheets with a few rows; a small press can read the pen-name column as an author column.
To replace the demo data: clear the yellow cells of the blank copy, paste your own rows and keep the formulas as they are. Nothing needs a macro or a login.

listing.title: Author Catalogue, Series Plan and Release Calendar Excel Template: Editions, Pre-order Planner, Price Checks, Format Wish List
listing.headline: Every title, edition and release date in one workbook, with conflicts flagged
listing.description:
Run the catalogue side of an author and self-publisher business in one Excel workbook. Built for an independent author who publishes under one or two pen names, often with a part-time assistant and freelancers paid per job, and for a small press that reads the pen-name column as an author column. Titles and Editions hold every book and every format with its list price, unit cost, royalty share, identifier, pages or finished hours and status. Series Plan Steps keeps the planned books of each series with planned release, planned cost and the read-through you expect into the next book.

The Release Calendar puts releases, pre-order openings, planned editions, price promotions and contractor deadlines in one list and flags two releases closer than your smallest gap. Release Gaps, Calendar by Month, Edition Completeness Check, Store Price List, Title Format Coverage, Format Wish List and Price per Page show gaps, busy months, missing or duplicated identifiers, store prices that differ from the list price, formats still missing and print cost shares. 18 tools answer the questions an author asks every week: is this release date free, when does each book of a series land, when must the next book start, which missing format adds the most copies, is the pre-order safe, are the prices consistent and which planned edition should be made first. Every tool ends in a plain verdict and a what-if table.

Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the assistant, editors, the cover designer, the formatter, narrators, the translator, the launch coordinator, the ad specialist, the web developer, the rights agent, the printer and yourself. This is part one of an eight-workbook suite for the Author and Self-Publisher Business. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros, no login and one flat price, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. It helps you keep track of your catalogue and plan your releases; it makes no promise of sales or income. Royalty shares, delays and tax points are your own numbers: check each store's current terms and confirm any tax point with your adviser.

paragraphs: Notice of {set:company}, dated {today}. Entry {col:calendar.entry_id}: {col:calendar.kind} for {col:calendar.title}.
The date is {col:calendar.date}, which is {col:calendar.days_from_today} days from today. Note: {col:calendar.note}.
Conflict check: {col:calendar.conflict}. If the date moves, every contractor deadline and the pre-order date move with it.
Please confirm that you have seen the new date and tell us at once if it breaks your plans.

documents.title: Catalogue audit report for one edition
paragraphs: Catalogue audit report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Edition {col:completeness.edition_id}: {col:completeness.title}, {col:completeness.format}, status {col:completeness.status}.

Identifier: {col:completeness.identifier}. Identifier missing: {col:completeness.id_missing}. Identifier used twice: {col:completeness.id_dup}. Price missing: {col:completeness.price_missing}. Pages or hours missing: {col:completeness.pages_missing}. Release date missing: {col:completeness.date_missing}.
Problems found: {col:completeness.problems}. Completeness: {col:completeness.completeness}. First problem: {col:completeness.issue}.
Fix every problem before the files are uploaded.
